description: Set up a decision log to record, review, and track the outcomes of key decisions over time.

steps.description: Define the schema for a decision log entry.

inputs.name: organization-context
inputs.desc: Type of organization and decision domains

outputs.name: decision-schema
outputs.desc: Field definitions for each log entry (date, decision, context, alternatives, rationale, owner, outcome)

outputs.name: entry-template
outputs.desc: Blank entry template ready to fill

process: List the fields every entry must carry (date, decision, context, alternatives considered, rationale, owner, expected outcome).
Add optional fields for tags, urgency, and reversibility.
Define the data types and validation rules for each field.
Produce the schema document and a blank entry template.

steps.description: Choose a storage format for the decision log.

inputs.name: team-size
inputs.desc: Number of people who will read and write entries

outputs.name: storage-format
outputs.desc: Chosen format (spreadsheet, database, markdown, wiki)

outputs.name: access-plan
outputs.desc: Who can read, who can write, where it lives

process: Evaluate storage options against the schema (spreadsheet, database, markdown files, wiki).
Match the option to team size and access patterns.
Define read and write permissions.
Document the chosen format and access plan.

steps.description: Establish the protocol for when and how to log decisions.

outputs.name: logging-protocol
outputs.desc: Rules for when to log, who logs, and how

outputs.name: trigger-checklist
outputs.desc: List of events that trigger a log entry

process: Define which decisions require logging (threshold: cost, reversibility, team impact).
Assign responsibility for logging (decision maker, delegate, or automated).
Set the timing (log before execution, within 24 hours, at next standup).
Produce the protocol document and trigger checklist.

steps.description: Set up periodic review of past decisions and their outcomes.

outputs.name: review-schedule
outputs.desc: When and how past decisions get reviewed

outputs.name: review-template
outputs.desc: Template for the review session

process: Set the review cadence (monthly, quarterly, at project close).
Define the review agenda (which decisions, what outcomes, what lessons).
Create the review session template.
Assign the review facilitator.

steps.description: Track decision outcomes over time and identify patterns.

outputs.name: outcome-tracker
outputs.desc: System for recording actual outcomes against expected outcomes

outputs.name: decision-log-framework
outputs.desc: Complete decision log framework document

process: Add outcome fields to each entry (actual outcome, variance from expected, date assessed).
Define the scoring criteria for decision quality.
Set up trend tracking (decision quality over time, by domain, by maker).
Produce the complete decision log framework.

description: Maintain an operations event ledger for recording, reviewing, and mining patterns from operational events.

steps.description: Define event types and severity levels for the ledger.

outputs.name: event-taxonomy
outputs.desc: Classified list of event types with severity levels

outputs.name: severity-definitions
outputs.desc: What each severity level means and how to assign it

process: List all operational event types (incidents, changes, decisions, milestones, exceptions).
Define severity levels (informational, warning, error, critical).
Map each event type to its default severity.
Produce the event taxonomy and severity definitions.

steps.description: Set up the recording protocol for ledger entries.

outputs.name: recording-protocol
outputs.desc: Rules for recording events (timestamp, type, description, actor, impact)

outputs.name: entry-template
outputs.desc: Template for a ledger entry

process: Define the required fields per entry (timestamp, event type, severity, description, actor, impact, resolution).
Set the recording timing (real-time for critical, batch for informational).
Create the entry template.
Document the recording protocol.

steps.description: Configure automated event capture where possible.

outputs.name: automation-plan
outputs.desc: Which events can be captured automatically and how

outputs.name: manual-capture-list
outputs.desc: Events that require manual recording

process: Identify events that can be captured from existing systems (CI/CD, monitoring, ticketing).
Design the integration for each automated source.
List events that remain manual and assign owners.
Produce the automation plan.

steps.description: Establish the review cadence for the ledger.

outputs.name: review-cadence
outputs.desc: Schedule and agenda for ledger reviews

outputs.name: escalation-rules
outputs.desc: When and how to escalate based on ledger patterns

process: Set the review frequency (daily scan, weekly review, monthly deep dive).
Define the review agenda for each frequency.
Set escalation rules (threshold triggers, pattern triggers).
Assign reviewers.

steps.description: Mine the ledger for patterns and produce the management plan.

outputs.name: pattern-analysis-method
outputs.desc: How to identify recurring patterns in the ledger

outputs.name: ledger-management-plan
outputs.desc: Complete ledger management plan

process: Define pattern categories (recurring events, correlated events, trending severity).
Set the analysis methods (frequency counts, time-series, correlation).
Define action thresholds (when a pattern triggers a process change).
Produce the complete ledger management plan.

description: Track guardrail enforcement events, measure violation frequency, and refine guardrails based on data.

steps.description: Inventory all guardrails and their trigger conditions.

inputs.name: guardrail-sources
inputs.desc: Where guardrails are defined (policies, code, configs)

inputs.name: operational-scope
inputs.desc: What systems and processes the guardrails cover

outputs.name: guardrail-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete list of guardrails with conditions and actions

outputs.name: guardrail-classification
outputs.desc: Guardrails classified by type (hard block, warning, audit-only)

process: Collect all guardrails from their source documents and systems.
For each guardrail, record the trigger condition, the enforced action, and the severity.
Classify each as hard block, warning, or audit-only.
Produce the guardrail inventory.

steps.description: Log each guardrail enforcement event.

outputs.name: enforcement-log-schema
outputs.desc: Schema for enforcement event records

outputs.name: logging-integration-plan
outputs.desc: How enforcement events get logged (automated and manual)

process: Define the enforcement event schema (timestamp, guardrail ID, trigger details, action taken, actor, outcome).
Identify which guardrails already emit logs and which need manual recording.
Design integrations for automated capture.
Produce the logging schema and integration plan.

steps.description: Track violation frequency by guardrail and identify the most-triggered rules.

outputs.name: frequency-report
outputs.desc: Violation frequency by guardrail, time period, and actor

outputs.name: top-triggered-list
outputs.desc: Ranked list of most-triggered guardrails

process: Count enforcement events per guardrail per time period.
Rank guardrails by trigger frequency.
Break down by actor, time of day, and context.
Produce the frequency report and top-triggered list.

steps.description: Review and update guardrails based on enforcement data.

outputs.name: guardrail-recommendations
outputs.desc: Recommendations to tighten, loosen, or retire guardrails

outputs.name: enforcement-report
outputs.desc: Complete guardrail enforcement report

process: Assess each high-frequency guardrail (is the rule too tight, or is the violation a real problem?).
Identify guardrails that never trigger (are they still needed, or is compliance universal?).
Draft recommendations (tighten, loosen, merge, retire, add new).
Produce the complete enforcement report.

description: Track project status across multiple workstreams with defined dimensions, update cadence, and escalation paths.

steps.description: Define the dimensions for tracking project status.

inputs.name: project-list
inputs.desc: Active projects or workstreams to track

outputs.name: tracking-dimensions
outputs.desc: Fields to track per workstream (milestone, owner, status, blockers, dependencies)

outputs.name: status-definitions
outputs.desc: What each status value means (on-track, at-risk, blocked, complete)

process: List the dimensions: milestone, owner, status, blockers, dependencies, next action, target date.
Define the status values and their criteria.
Map stakeholder needs to tracking dimensions.
Produce the tracking dimension definitions.

steps.description: Set the update cadence and collection method.

outputs.name: update-cadence
outputs.desc: How often updates are collected and from whom

outputs.name: collection-method
outputs.desc: How updates are gathered (form, meeting, async, automated)

process: Set the update frequency by project criticality (daily for critical, weekly for standard).
Choose the collection method (async form, standup, status meeting, automated from tools).
Assign update owners per workstream.
Produce the cadence and collection plan.

steps.description: Identify at-risk items and escalate blockers.

outputs.name: risk-criteria
outputs.desc: Rules for flagging items as at-risk

outputs.name: escalation-protocol
outputs.desc: How and when blockers get escalated

process: Define at-risk criteria (missed milestones, stale updates, unresolved blockers for N days).
Set the escalation path (owner, manager, steering committee).
Define the escalation timing and format.
Produce the risk criteria and escalation protocol.

steps.description: Generate the project status report.

outputs.name: report-template
outputs.desc: Template for the status report

outputs.name: project-status-report
outputs.desc: Complete project status report framework

process: Design the report layout (summary, per-workstream detail, blockers, actions).
Include risk flags and escalation status.
Set the distribution list and format.
Produce the report template and framework.

description: Log changes, track their downstream effects, and identify patterns of unintended consequences.

steps.description: Design the change record schema.

inputs.name: change-domains
inputs.desc: What types of changes to track (code, process, policy, infrastructure)

outputs.name: change-record-schema
outputs.desc: Fields for each change entry (what, who, when, why, scope, expected impact)

outputs.name: change-template
outputs.desc: Blank change record template

process: Define the change record fields: what changed, who made the change, timestamp, rationale, expected impact, scope.
Add fields for downstream tracking: actual impact, incidents linked, rollback status.
Create the change record template.
Document the schema.

steps.description: Track downstream effects of each change.

outputs.name: effect-tracking-method
outputs.desc: How downstream effects are identified and recorded

outputs.name: linkage-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for linking changes to incidents or improvements

process: Define what counts as a downstream effect (incident, performance change, user complaint, improvement).
Set the observation window per change type (24 hours, 1 week, 1 month).
Create the linkage rules (how to associate an effect with its cause).
Document the tracking method.

steps.description: Identify unintended consequences from change data.

outputs.name: consequence-patterns
outputs.desc: Recurring unintended consequence patterns

outputs.name: prevention-recommendations
outputs.desc: How to prevent the identified patterns

process: Analyze linked effects to find negative outcomes not in the expected impact.
Categorize unintended consequences (performance, usability, cost, security).
Identify recurring patterns (same type of change producing the same type of consequence).
Produce prevention recommendations.

steps.description: Produce the change impact report.

outputs.name: change-impact-report
outputs.desc: Complete change impact report with patterns and recommendations

outputs.name: process-improvement-actions
outputs.desc: Specific actions to improve the change process

process: Summarize all changes, their effects, and any unintended consequences.
Highlight the top recurring patterns.
List prevention recommendations ranked by impact.
Produce the change impact report and process improvement actions.

description: Maintain a lessons learned register that captures, categorizes, and tracks adoption of lessons from projects and operations.

steps.description: Define when and how lessons are captured.

inputs.name: team-structure
inputs.desc: Who participates in lessons learned sessions

outputs.name: capture-protocol
outputs.desc: Rules for when to capture lessons (milestones, project close, incidents)

outputs.name: lesson-template
outputs.desc: Template for recording a lesson (what happened, what was learned, action)

process: Define the capture points: project milestones, project close, post-incident, quarterly review.
Design the lesson template (context, what happened, what was learned, recommended action, owner).
Assign facilitators for each capture point.
Document the capture protocol.

steps.description: Categorize lessons by theme for pattern analysis.

outputs.name: category-taxonomy
outputs.desc: Lesson categories (process, technical, communication, estimation, tooling)

outputs.name: tagging-rules
outputs.desc: How to assign categories to each lesson

process: Define the top-level categories: process, technical, communication, estimation, tooling, people.
Add subcategories where needed.
Write the tagging rules (one primary category, up to two secondary).
Produce the taxonomy and tagging rules.

steps.description: Assess which lessons are actionable and assign follow-up.

outputs.name: action-plan
outputs.desc: Actionable lessons with owners, deadlines, and expected outcomes

outputs.name: non-actionable-archive
outputs.desc: Lessons noted but not requiring action (context for future reference)

process: For each lesson, assess whether it is actionable (can a specific change prevent recurrence?).
For actionable lessons, assign an owner, deadline, and expected outcome.
Archive non-actionable lessons for reference.
Produce the action plan.

steps.description: Track whether lessons are adopted and measure improvement.

outputs.name: adoption-metrics
outputs.desc: Completion rate and recurrence rate for actioned lessons

outputs.name: lessons-learned-report
outputs.desc: Complete lessons learned report

process: Track action completion status (done, in progress, overdue, dropped).
Measure whether the same lesson recurs (recurrence = adoption failure).
Aggregate by category to find systemic gaps.
Produce the complete lessons learned report.

description: Set up a KPI tracking dashboard aligned to business objectives with targets, thresholds, and alerting.

steps.description: Define KPIs aligned to business objectives.

outputs.name: kpi-list
outputs.desc: Defined KPIs with formulas, owners, and update frequency

outputs.name: objective-alignment-map
outputs.desc: Map of each KPI to the objective it measures

process: For each business objective, identify one to three KPIs that measure progress.
Define each KPI: name, formula, data source, owner, update frequency.
Map each KPI to its parent objective.
Produce the KPI list and alignment map.

steps.description: Identify and connect data sources for each KPI.

outputs.name: data-source-map
outputs.desc: Each KPI matched to its data source and extraction method

outputs.name: data-gap-list
outputs.desc: KPIs where data is not yet available

process: Match each KPI to its data source (database, API, spreadsheet, manual entry).
Define the extraction method and refresh schedule.
Identify KPIs with no available data source and plan how to close the gap.
Produce the data source map and gap list.

steps.description: Set targets and alerting thresholds for each KPI.

outputs.name: targets-and-thresholds
outputs.desc: Target value, warning threshold, and critical threshold per KPI

outputs.name: alert-rules
outputs.desc: When and how alerts fire

process: Set the target value for each KPI based on business goals.
Set warning and critical thresholds (percent deviation from target, absolute value, trend direction).
Define who receives alerts and through what channel.
Produce the targets, thresholds, and alert rules.

steps.description: Build the dashboard layout and produce the KPI dashboard plan.

outputs.name: dashboard-layout
outputs.desc: Dashboard wireframe with KPI placement and visualization types

outputs.name: kpi-dashboard-plan
outputs.desc: Complete KPI dashboard plan

process: Group KPIs by objective or function.
Select the visualization type per KPI (gauge, time series, bar chart, number with trend arrow).
Lay out the dashboard (summary row, detail sections, drill-down links).
Produce the complete KPI dashboard plan.

description: Track actions from retrospectives, measure completion, and identify recurring themes.

steps.description: Capture action items from retrospectives with owners and deadlines.

inputs.name: team-roster
inputs.desc: Team members available to own actions

outputs.name: action-items
outputs.desc: List of actions with owner, deadline, and category

outputs.name: theme-tags
outputs.desc: Themes identified in the retrospective

process: Extract every action item from the retro notes.
Assign an owner and deadline to each.
Tag each action by theme (process, tooling, communication, workload, quality).
Produce the action list and theme tags.

steps.description: Track completion status and surface carry-over items.

outputs.name: completion-status
outputs.desc: Status of each action (done, in progress, overdue, dropped)

outputs.name: carry-over-list
outputs.desc: Actions not completed, carried to the next sprint

process: Check each action against its deadline.
Classify as done, in progress, overdue, or dropped.
Flag carry-over items (actions surviving more than one retro cycle).
Produce the completion status and carry-over list.

steps.description: Measure improvement trends over time and produce the retro action report.

outputs.name: improvement-trends
outputs.desc: Trends in action completion rate, recurring themes, and carry-over rate

outputs.name: retro-action-report
outputs.desc: Complete retrospective action report

process: Calculate the completion rate per sprint.
Identify themes with the most carry-over (systemic issues).
Track improvement trends over the last N sprints.
Produce the complete retro action report.

description: Design an audit trail system with immutable records, retention policies, and a query interface.

steps.description: Define which events require an audit record.

inputs.name: system-scope
inputs.desc: Systems and processes to be audited

inputs.name: compliance-requirements
inputs.desc: Regulatory and policy requirements for audit trails

outputs.name: auditable-events
outputs.desc: List of events that must produce an audit record

outputs.name: audit-trigger-rules
outputs.desc: Conditions that trigger an audit entry

process: List all user actions, system actions, and data changes in scope.
Map regulatory requirements to specific events.
Define trigger rules for each auditable event.
Produce the auditable events list and trigger rules.

steps.description: Specify the record schema for each audit entry.

outputs.name: audit-record-schema
outputs.desc: Field definitions (who, what, when, where, before value, after value)

outputs.name: schema-validation-rules
outputs.desc: Validation rules for each field

process: Define the standard fields: actor, action, timestamp, resource, before-state, after-state, source IP, session ID.
Add compliance-specific fields as required.
Set validation rules (non-null actor, valid timestamp format, referential integrity).
Produce the schema and validation rules.

steps.description: Design immutable storage and retention policies.

outputs.name: storage-design
outputs.desc: Immutable storage architecture (append-only, hash chain, WORM)

outputs.name: retention-policy
outputs.desc: How long records are kept and when they are purged

process: Select the immutability mechanism (append-only log, hash chain, WORM storage).
Define the retention periods by event type and regulation.
Plan the archival and purge process.
Produce the storage design and retention policy.

steps.description: Build the query interface and produce the audit trail design document.

outputs.name: query-interface-spec
outputs.desc: Specification for searching and filtering audit records

outputs.name: audit-trail-design-document
outputs.desc: Complete audit trail design document

process: Define the query dimensions (by actor, by resource, by time range, by action type).
Design the search interface (API, dashboard, CLI).
Set access controls for who can query audit records.
Produce the complete audit trail design document.

description: Set up a multi-level operational review cadence from daily standups through quarterly strategy reviews.

steps.description: Define the review levels and their purposes.

outputs.name: review-levels
outputs.desc: Defined levels (daily standup, weekly ops, monthly business, quarterly strategy)

outputs.name: level-purposes
outputs.desc: What each level is for and what it is not for

process: Define each review level: daily (execution), weekly (operations), monthly (business health), quarterly (strategy).
Set the purpose and non-purpose of each level.
Map existing meetings to the levels.
Produce the review level definitions.

steps.description: Set the agenda and metrics for each review level.

outputs.name: agendas
outputs.desc: Standard agenda for each review level

outputs.name: metrics-per-level
outputs.desc: Which metrics are reviewed at which level

process: Write the standard agenda for each level (time-boxed, with roles: facilitator, note-taker, decision-maker).
Assign metrics to each level (daily: blockers and WIP; weekly: throughput and risks; monthly: P&L and pipeline; quarterly: OKRs and strategy).
Set time limits for each agenda item.
Produce the agendas and metrics assignments.

steps.description: Design the escalation path between review levels.

outputs.name: escalation-rules
outputs.desc: When and how items escalate from one level to the next

outputs.name: de-escalation-rules
outputs.desc: When items drop back to a lower level

process: Define escalation triggers (unresolved after N days, exceeds budget threshold, cross-team dependency).
Map each trigger to its target level.
Define de-escalation criteria (resolved, within tolerance, owner accepted).
Produce the escalation and de-escalation rules.

steps.description: Track action items across all review levels and produce the cadence framework.

outputs.name: action-tracking-system
outputs.desc: How actions are tracked across levels (single backlog, linked registers)

outputs.name: review-cadence-framework
outputs.desc: Complete operational review cadence framework

process: Design the action tracking system (one backlog with level tags, or linked registers per level).
Set the review-of-reviews mechanism (quarterly review assesses whether the cadence itself works).
Assign facilitators for each level.
Produce the complete review cadence framework.
